verdict.probe_answer: Arm A: yes. It identifies the gawk `load` variable-name collision, fixes only `scripts/test-db/select_db_host.sh`, and leaves `test/hooks.js` untouched. Arm B: yes. It makes the same minimal variable rename in the DB-host script only, and leaves `test/hooks.js` untouched.
verdict.rationale: Both arms fix the actual pipeline failure by avoiding `awk -v load=...`, which GNU awk rejects because `load` is a builtin. Both are minimal, confined to `scripts/test-db/select_db_host.sh`, and do not touch the unrelated transaction-hook code. Arm A adds a clarifying comment and uses `loadavg`; Arm B uses `ld`. That readability difference is not material. Neither diff includes tests, so test strength is parity.
